text.p: These are the leading stories in the Malawi press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Eight opposition parties not represented in parliament on Sunday teamed up to form a party to be called United Council for Dialogue (UCD). The eight said they have formed UCD because Malawi is in danger of drifting into anarchy.
- The Lilongwe City Council in the capital, is from today launching a 16-day shooting and vaccination campaign of dogs to control rabies.
- Government is to spend five million Malawi kwacha tax payers' funds on special assistants for cabinet ministers.

- Former second Vice President Chakufwa Chihana who is also president for opposition Alliance for Democracy says he feels sorry for the people because president Bakili Muluzi has distanced himself from them.
